citation: F. Shimizu, "Frequency broadening in liquids by a short light pulse", Phys. Rev. Lett. 19(19), 1097-1100 (6 Nov 1967)
fullTextRead: Yes. The PDF (5 pages; pages 1 and 4-5 hold other papers of the same issue) has a text layer from OCR that is garbled in places (exponents, minus signs). It was read through that text layer (PyMuPDF; the Read tool's PDF mode needs pdftoppm, which is not installed) and every quoted number and equation was confirmed on rendered page images (pp. 1098 and 1099). Fig. 1 is a photograph of spectra: only its scale bar (100 cm^-1) and the 6943 A label are used. The PDF is not in the repository.
topic: self-phase modulation with a finite relaxation time: low-frequency-side broadening and periodic spectral structure of filaments in CS2

referenceNumbers.value: Q-switched ruby laser, 694.3 nm (6943 A), beam diameter 3 mm, CS2 cell 7.5 cm; laser = 4-5 groups of axial modes
dphi = -(k0/n0) L dn; dn = (n2/tau) int_-inf^t <E^2>(t') exp(-(t-t')/tau) dt'
tau = 0: shift ~ -d<E^2>/dt, broadening on both sides; tau large: shift ~ -<E^2>, broadening only on the low-frequency side
regular periodic structure on the low-frequency side; period 10 +- 3 cm^-1 on average, increasing linearly with the distance from the centre
ratio between intensity maxima and minima at least 10
about 90 % of the energy on the low-frequency side; intensity roughly uniform there with a maximum at the low-frequency extremity; also a peak at the laser frequency
periodic structure with larger spacing also on the high-frequency side (if tau is short enough compared with the pulse)
power spectrum I1^2 + I2^2 + 2 I1 I2 cos(psi2 - psi1), psi2 - psi1 = (dphi(t2) - dphi(t1)) - (t2 - t1) d(omega); t1, t2 where d(dphi)/dt = d(omega)
filament duration ~ the inverse of the average period, given as 6e-12 s
referenceNumbers.status: verified; note 1/(c 10 cm^-1) = 3.3 ps, not 6 ps

referenceNumbers.value: broadening at most 5 % of the laser frequency; Raman shift of CS2 656 cm^-1 not given in the paper (smaller-than-Raman-shift condition is stated)

assumptions: Not in the paper: n2, intensity, filament size, relaxation time tau, pulse shape. Used here: Gaussian pulse, FWHM 6 ps (the paper's own inferred duration), tau = 2 ps (literature orientational relaxation of CS2; UNVERIFIED, not from the paper) plus a scan of tau, peak phase of the stationary response B = 120 rad (chosen to give ~100-150 cm^-1 of broadening, the order of the scale bar; it is a free parameter of the experiment).
1-D plane wave: the filament (self-trapped beam) is not modelled; the paper too treats only phase modulation in the lowest order (intensity envelope undistorted).

CS2: the main run uses a user material (Kedenburg et al. 2012 index via refractiveindex.info, not from the paper; n2 = 3e-19 m2/W only sets the intensity scale) with a single-exponential user delayed response h(t) = exp(-t/tau)/tau, fR = 1, because that is the paper's model. A second run uses the built-in material CS2 (orientational response 0.2/1.6 ps, fR 0.9, n2 3e-18; UNVERIFIED typical values, docs/reference/materials.md).
The delayed response needs a window that holds its memory (circular convolution); the auto grid now adds it (2026-11 fix), a too-short fixed window warns.
The mode structure of the ruby laser (the pulse is not a smooth Gaussian) is not modelled.
